main_text.p: Ventriculi cordis sunt duo, dexter & sinister.

Dexter ventriculus cordis est in dextra parte ejus magis, quodammodo deorsum ad cordis mucronem, instar falcatae Lunae vergens, sanguinem receptum e-laboratius excoquens, & extenuans suo calore.Dexter.
In dextrum cordis Thalamum infigitur vena cava, & vena arterialis, illa sanguinem ex epate affert; haec coctum jam e corde in pulmones effert.
Sinister ventriculus (qui tamen in medio cordis conspicitur) instar coni ar-ctum versus mucronem paulatim desinens, officina & promtuariu[?] est spirituum vitalium.Sinister.
E sinistro ventriculo oritur cum ar-teria aorta, tum arteria venalis.Arteria aorta.Arteria venalis.
Illa arteriarum truncus maximus e corde arteriosum sanguinem & spiritum vitalem excipit & evehit: haec dicitur aërem extrinsecus advenientem e pulmonibus in sinistrum ventriculum transmittere.
Hi ventriculi distinguuntur medio septo satis crasso, multisq; foraminibus

page.notes: Right margin notes: "Dexter.", "Sinister.", "Arteria aorta.", "Arteria venalis." Faint show-through text from the reverse page was omitted. Doubtful readings marked [?]: "promtuariu" (probably promtuarium/promtuarii with a superscript mark) and "ventriculum" was read as printed. The catchword "per-" is the start of the next page's first word.
